title: Span proxy multiplexer for backend-agnostic tracing exports
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight in-cluster span proxy (multiplexer) that accepts OpenTelemetry spans from our instrumented services and routes/rewrites them to one or more tracing backends (Tempo, Jaeger, third-party SaaS) without requiring changes to downstream exporters. The proxy should enable per-tenant backend mapping, per-route sampling annotations passthrough, and minimal added latency.

Scope:
- Ingest OTLP/HTTP and OTLP/gRPC span batches.
- Support routing rules: tenant-based, service-name overrides, and environment tags.
- Translate and forward to backend-specific endpoints (Tempo-compatible HTTP, Jaeger thrift/HTTP where required) using pluggable adapters.
- Preserve span IDs/trace IDs and canonicalize resource attributes for downstream retention policies.
- Implement adaptive batching and backpressure (bounded queue, 200ms max holding time).
- Graceful degradation: when a backend is unavailable the proxy buffers to S3-like storage for up to 24h and switches to fallback backend per policy.
- Observability: internal metrics (ingest rate, export latency P50/P95/P99, dropped spans, buffer occupancy) and tracing for the proxy itself.

Non-goals:
- Full replacement of existing exporters in SDKs. SDK changes are out of scope for this ticket.
- Long-term multi-TLS client auth; initial rollout uses mTLS to selected backends only.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Proxy accepts 10k spans/sec sustained with <1.5ms median added latency and P99 added latency <15ms in test harness.
2) Correct routing for tenant-based rules in integration test suite.
3) Successful translation to Tempo HTTP format and to Jaeger HTTP endpoints in end-to-end test env.
4) Metrics exported to the Redwood metrics stack and dashboards updated.
5) Rollout plan with canary and automatic fallback documented in Confluence.

Design notes:
- Use lightweight Go service colocated with ingress pods behind service mesh.
- Adapters implement an interface with Transform(batch)->[]backendRequests to allow future backends.
- Use lock-free queues (channel-backed ring buffer) and a small worker pool for concurrency.
- Adaptive batching parameters (maxBatchBytes, maxBatchSpans, maxWaitMs) tunable per tenant via ConfigMap/Control Plane.
- For storage-on-failure use pre-existing object-store signer and retention lifecycle.

Deliverables:
- Code + unit/integration tests in observability repo.
- Grafana dashboards and alert rules.
- Confluence design + rollout checklist.
- Canary and full rollout runbook.
